title: A measure of care for both

captions.physics: Creating warm conditions in daily life
captions.emotions: Feeling the fairness of mutual care

meaning: You can care for each other fairly when different needs are brought together without requiring identical responses.
text: Tenderness sometimes needs a fitting measure, especially when your wishes differ. In the physical position of Anahata, the Empress gives care a tangible form through comforts, small gifts and time prepared for being together. Temperance in energy directs attention towards combining different needs: you want a kind of involvement that leaves neither of you displaced. Justice in emotions brings satisfaction in an honest exchange. Support becomes easier to receive when there is understandable agreement behind it and different wishes do not become evidence that one person loves less.

For example, one of you enjoys unexpected visitors while the other values a quiet day off. You agree on a short daytime visit and keep the evening free. **Care becomes fair when it considers what comfort costs each person.** You can prepare refreshments together without making the entire day follow someone else’s programme. Warmth is felt in both the welcome and the quiet afterwards: each part of the day has grown from real attention to you both.

The difficulty begins when a useful proportion is treated as a permanent law. Every visit must last the same time, each concession needs precise compensation, and a changed request seems unfair. Agreement becomes measurement, leaving a living wish difficult to include in the calculation. Fairness keeps its tenderness when circumstances can be heard again alongside the earlier arrangement, rather than only checking whether its terms were followed.
